title: Synergy of strength–ductility in HfMoTaTiZr refractory high entropy alloy through Cr addition

recollection.starting_material: Guess: A base refractory high-entropy alloy composed of Hf, Mo, Ta, Ti, and Zr.
recollection.intervention: Guess: They added chromium (Cr) to the base refractory high-entropy alloy in various amounts to study its effect on mechanical properties.
recollection.structure: Guess: The resulting alloy likely remained primarily a body-centered cubic (BCC) solid-solution phase, potentially refined by the Cr addition.
recollection.mechanism: Guess: The addition of Cr introduced atomic-scale lattice distortions and possibly altered phase stability, resulting in combined solid-solution strengthening and improved ductility through dislocation interactions.
recollection.results: Guess: The main finding was that moderate Cr additions enhanced both strength (likely exceeding 1000 MPa yield strength) and ductility (tensile elongation improved compared to the Cr-free alloy), leading to a notable synergy in mechanical performance.

score.note: Correctly identifies Cr addition, but gives no specific 4.2 at.% composition or processing details. The structure recollection misses the key interconnected Cr₂(Ti,Zr,Hf,Ta) Laves phase and instead speculates about BCC retention/refinement. It correctly mentions lattice-distortion-based solid-solution strengthening, but misses the Laves-network crack-hindrance and plasticity-compensation mechanism. Quantitative outcomes are vague and do not closely reproduce the reported 1750.6 MPa yield strength, 14.0% fracture strain, 3.8% Laves fraction, or 535.8 HV0.3 hardness.
